value.first: Six months is the right window, and the green light is really about signs he's ready: sitting with support, steady head, and reaching for your food. Week 1: pick one meal a day when he's happy, not starving. Offer a couple of teaspoons of something smooth and iron-rich, like iron-fortified cereal thinned with milk, or well-mashed avocado. Expect most of it to come back out. That's normal - the first weeks are practice, not nutrition.
value.second: Weeks 2-3: build to two meals a day and widen the menu - pureed or soft-mashed veg, fruit, and pieces of meat or lentils for iron. Introduce one new single food at a time, a few days apart, so if a reaction shows up you know the culprit. Don't skip the common allergens - smooth peanut butter thinned with water, egg, dairy - offering them early and often is what the research now points to. Milk stays his main food for now; solids are alongside it.
value.third: By week 4 you're aiming for two or three small meals daily, and he's better at moving food to the back of his mouth. Let him get messy with soft finger foods - it builds the chewing and pincer grip coming next. You'll know it's working when he opens for the spoon and gags less over time. Gagging is loud but normal; silent, floppy, or blue is choking and different. If he flat-out refuses all solids after a few weeks, or you see hives, swelling, or vomiting after a food, worth raising with your doctor.
